races.name: Available Car Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Champagne Charlee
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams yard sends two unexposed runners, this one carrying top weight with unknown running style — lightly raced and unquantified, so any pace map placement is speculative; treat as a wildcard with no meaningful form data.|
runners_data.comment: An 8,000gns colt by Profitable, making his debut out of a dam who showed modest form at seven furlongs as a two-year-old; his half-brother Evelyn's Phoenix was fair at nine furlongs, and while this looks a tough opening assignment, there's pedigree substance to work with.

runners_data.name: Dreamlover
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who showed smart form on debut but steps up from 5f to 6f; headgear (blinkers) likely to sharpen early pace, and with two others fighting for the same position the battle for lead may prove costly to stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a maiden at Chester last time, beaten six and a half lengths in first-time blinkers, matched his level on debut and now drops in grade; effective at today's trip on a sound surface, and with the yard in form, he's an obvious threat here.

runners_data.name: Dream On Kent
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 6f on good ground and acts on this surface reliably, but Pat Cosgrave will find Havana Gift and Dreamlover equally determined to lead; a second or third position would actually suit better but this horse's instinct is to hit the front from flag-fall.|
runners_data.comment: A close second in a novice at Chepstow last time, wearing a visor down to six furlongs, adds to another runner-up effort in his last three starts; well suited by this trip and ground, and with the yard having landed this race twelve months ago, he holds solid claims dropping in company.

runners_data.name: Little Mester
runners_data.note: Second Williams unknown quantity on the day — no style classification, no prior form to decode; shares a trainer pattern with stablemate Champagne Charlee and both could be anything, but unraced or lightly raced horses face a steep task in a field with pace exposure.|
runners_data.comment: A gelding by Mohaather making his racecourse debut, out of a dam who was fair form at fourteen furlongs; his half-brother Claim That Smile showed fair form at six furlongs, though this is no easy starting point at this level, leaving him with more to prove than the leading names.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been placed on similar good ground at 5f but now faces 6f with a contested pace — should get a race to run at, but the form figures (5,9) suggest a horse still learning rather than one ready to win; Richard Hughes yard has good recent strike rate.|
runners_data.comment: A debut ninth was followed by an improved fifth at the minimum trip last time, beaten six and a quarter lengths in a maiden at this course; first-time blinkers and another drop in grade could help, but the yard's cold recent form, two winners from forty-five runners, leaves him the outsider on our figures.

runners_data.name: Tamam Star
runners_data.note: K R Burke's consistent place-getter has hit the frame four times in seven starts, all on good ground, and a prominent tracking style means this horse is perfectly placed to exploit the three-way pace battle up front; 22 days fresh, apprentice claim from Jack Nicholls (5) adds minor interest.|
runners_data.comment: Having underperformed in a seller at York last time, beaten nine lengths, this colt followed two thirds and a fourth and should have gone closer there; back at this trip on the sound surface he prefers, and our top-rated runner in this field, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.note: David Allan and Tim Easterby combine on a horse who has placed seven times in seven career runs on good ground — extraordinary consistency but no win yet suggests a horse who finishes into places rather than winning, and a strongly-run race gives the best chance of finding a rival to run down.|
runners_data.comment: Third in four of his last six starts, most recently over five furlongs at Musselburgh when beaten three and a quarter lengths in a maiden, this colt races consistently around this level and is at home on a sound surface; with a big weight to carry the only obvious concern, he ranks a leading threat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: David Evans runner stepping back from 7f to 6f after a single debut run — hold-up style on similar going, and the shorter trip in a fast race should theoretically suit better; Ryan Kavanagh (5) claim is noted but the horse's class is unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth on his only start to date, never featuring after a slow start when beaten seven lengths in a maiden at this course, this gelding needs much more back down in trip and grade; the yard was successful in this race last year, but there's little in the form itself to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Yankeedoodledandy
runners_data.note: Form figure of 0 (last of 13) on debut on identical going is deeply unpromising; tagged as a horse who fades in the finish which is the worst possible profile for a race with maximum early pace — chances appear minimal unless debut was a significant experience run.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a maiden at Windsor on her only start, hampered and never able to get competitive, this filly clearly needs a big step forward; she does have experience over today's trip and going, but on that solitary effort a major turnaround looks necessary to feature.

runners_data.name: Havana Gift
runners_data.note: Racing just two days after last run suggests Quinn yard believes this horse is in fine fettle; a confirmed front-runner who has won a race over 5f and placed on good ground, stepping up to 6f represents an unknown stamina question when carrying the pace hard against two rivals doing the same.|
runners_data.comment: A fourth in a nursery at Nottingham latest, beaten two and a quarter lengths, continues a run of competitive placed efforts, including a second two starts back; light-framed and claiming off a workable mark, she reappears quickly just two days on and is well suited by this trip on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Beach Ahead
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and wearing a tongue-tie, Beach Ahead has posted two fourth-place finishes including one on good ground over 6f — David Probert is a quality booking and the unknown style tag means this horse could emerge from midfield if the pace carnage opens a route through.|
runners_data.comment: Twice fourth in his last two starts, this colt was dropped in grade on softer ground when beaten three and a half lengths in a seller at Goodwood latest, and stepping back to six furlongs, where he's shown his form, should suit; our rating has him firmly in the mix, though a big weight and first-time tongue-tie leave a couple of questions.

races.paceDynamic: Havana Gift, Dreamlover, and Dream On Kent are all confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field over 6f at Leicester on good-to-firm ground, guaranteeing a strong early gallop from the outset with three horses competing aggressively for the lead. This contested pace will stretch the field within the first furlong, and with none of the three likely to concede position willingly, the leader will almost certainly be setting a genuine tempo rather than a tactical crawl. The race shape that emerges — a hard-run six furlongs on a fast surface — classically favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a prominent or handy position and pounce in the final two furlongs rather than those who either burn themselves out fighting for the lead or those forced to make up ground from too far back. Prominent runners with tactical speed, specifically Tamam Star and any horse capable of tracking from a close second or third, are best placed by this shape; true hold-up horses like Turnstile, South West, and Vinery face a stern test of their ability to close a gap that a fast pace does open but a sprint finish may shut just as quickly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead burns all protagonists out by halfway, creating a genuine pace collapse.
scenarios.body: Havana Gift, Dreamlover and Dream On Kent fight each other to exhaustion through the first three furlongs, leaving a yawning gap for horses tracking in the first three or four off the pace to sweep through; the good-to-firm ground helps hold-up horses close the distance quickly in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners breaks quickest and the others drop off, allowing a lone leader to control tempo.
scenarios.body: Should Havana Gift or Dream On Kent clear the opposition early and establish a rhythm-dictating lead, they may convert raw pace into a front-running win with stamina reserves intact; a controlled gallop removes the burnout risk and rewards the horse with the highest natural cruising speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent runner settles just behind the pace battle and produces a well-timed turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Tamam Star, with consistent place-hitting form and a prominent style, is the archetype for this scenario — sitting third or fourth through the early chaos before finding room inside the final two furlongs; on good-to-firm ground with a pace to chase, a horse who has shown repetitive late-finishing speed in similar conditions can win decisively.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and enough daylight opens for genuine hold-up runners to reel in the field late.
scenarios.body: Turnstile has posted consistent placed efforts in similar ground and distances and Vinery represents the unknown quality from a big-race yard, both needing maximum early pace and a very straight run through to deliver; this is the least likely shape to fully materialise because the front-runners would need to completely capitulate while the closer finds a clean passage in a bunched field.

watchPoints.text: Tamam Star — if Jack Nicholls slots this horse cleanly into fourth or fifth early with the pace battle raging ahead, K R Burke's consistent performer has the profile to arrive late and powerfully in the final furlong.

Havana Gift — running just two days after last outing is a notable freshness risk; if any staleness surfaces through the early three-way pace battle at 6f, this horse may empty before the line despite natural front-running ability.

Turnstile — David Allan will need to find a clean passage through what will likely be a compressed mid-race group; seven placed efforts without a win suggests a horse that requires everything to fall right, and congestion at the two-furlong pole could deny the run.

Dream On Kent and Dreamlover — both wear headgear (blinkers) which will sharpen early speed further; monitor the draw and early positions closely at the start, as whichever of the three front-runners breaks sharpest will likely dictate the race shape more than the others.

Champagne Charlee and Little Mester — two completely unknown Stuart Williams runners; if either is well-supported in the market before the off, treat as a possible significant form or trial run being unveiled here.

races.name: Smooth Radio EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Anyasi
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's OR-120 filly has winning form over 6f on soft ground and placed at 7f on good, giving her solid course-relevant experience; sole front-runner in this field and expected to dictate fully unopposed, which plays directly to her strengths on good-to-firm.|
runners_data.comment: A clear improver from his debut effort, this colt got off the mark at Yarmouth last time, scoring by three lengths in a novice, and there should be more to come even under a penalty today; with the stable in good form and conditions on the soft side well within his compass, he's taken to follow up.

runners_data.name: Bucklow Hill
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner returning after 71 days off, so fitness is the key question; won over 6f at Sandown on a flat track and placed once in two runs on similar going, suggesting the conditions suit, but the layoff makes him a slight unknown at the head of affairs.|
runners_data.comment: A big, strong sort who could only manage a well-beaten effort down the field in a novice at Doncaster most recently, some way below the level he showed when getting off the mark previously, this colt returns off a lengthy break with a first-time tongue-tie fitted, and there's a good chance he can return to that level of form; the six-furlong trip and an all-weather surface both look right up his street.

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3-year-old won over 6f on soft and placed at 7f on good, with a trainer 14-day record of 5/32 suggesting a steady yard in decent form; likely to press Anyasi throughout and his recent experience gives him a solid profile for this straightforward contest.|
runners_data.comment: Showing plenty of resolve, this gelding improved on a third-placed debut to get off the mark by a narrow margin in a novice at Catterick last time over six furlongs, and there's no reason he can't follow up back at a similar trip; he's versatile on good-to-soft or good-to-firm ground and rates capable of another bold showing.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's lightly-raced type (tagged for limited experience) has shown only modest efforts in two starts, finishing 7th and 10th, and his unquantified running style makes him a genuine unknown; the small team's T14 of 0/4 does nothing to encourage confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Two runs so far have brought little in the way of encouragement, with performances well below what's needed at this level, and there's a growing sense that a step up to middle distances is required rather than today's sprint trip; on what he's shown to date, a case for involvement here is hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Baby G
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's filly is one-dimensional based on her sole run — an 8th over 5f at Sandown — and is flagged as fading in the finish, which is a clear concern stepping up to 6f against more experienced rivals; the Carroll yard has been active (T14 8/52) but this runner lacks the form to inspire.|
runners_data.comment: A slow start effectively ended her chance in a maiden at Wolverhampton on her only outing, and she was never involved from there, finishing a well-beaten eighth; a significant step forward is needed on that solitary piece of form to trouble this field.

runners_data.name: Material Girl
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner has a pair of 5th and 7th finishes on similar surfaces, suggesting she is competitive but not threatening at this level; as a prominent type she will be involved early but her recent form trend heading the wrong way makes her a place-rather-than-win proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held in a novice at Southwell last time, matching much the same level shown on debut, this filly looks exposed already and leaves plenty to find on what she's shown; the yard is also out of form, with just a single winner from thirty-four runners in the last fortnight, adding to the case against her at six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Red Legs
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's hold-up operator has two finishes of 7th and 8th over this exact course-and-distance profile on soft and good, making her the least likely to benefit from what looks set to be a steadily-run race where the front groups are given a soft lead throughout.|
runners_data.comment: A step forward from a poor debut still left her closer to last than midfield when beaten ten lengths in a novice at Yarmouth last time, and there remains plenty of improvement required; bred with a mile very much in mind long-term, today's six furlongs may not be doing her any favours just yet.

races.paceDynamic: Anyasi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven over 6f on good-to-firm ground at Leicester, and with no other horse in the race carrying a clear lead-from-the-front profile, she will dictate terms entirely unchallenged from the off. Bucklow Hill, Two Commanders, and Material Girl are all prominent types who will track behind her in the early stages, creating a conventional prominent pack rather than any pressure on the leader. With pace uncontested, Anyasi is likely to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo, keeping something in reserve for the final furlong rather than burning energy fighting for position. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racers who can travel close to the pace throughout — hold-up horses like Red Legs face the additional burden of finding a clear run late when the race may already be decided up front on a flat course that rarely sees dramatic late swoops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Anyasi Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Anyasi leads cleanly and sets a fair but manageable pace, drawing on her class advantage at OR 120.
scenarios.body: Anyasi dictates from flag to finish on good-to-firm ground that suits her form profile, using the freedom of an uncontested lead to conserve energy before stretching clear inside the final furlong. Prominent runners tracking her closely — Two Commanders and Bucklow Hill — are the most likely to pick up any pieces if she tires, but her class edge makes her the primary beneficiary of this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Anyasi sets a fraction too quick early and the prominent pair pressing her capitalise on her fading in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Two Commanders or Bucklow Hill, travelling comfortably just off the pace, time their challenge to arrive in the final furlong as Anyasi's uncontested lead comes back to them. Both have decent recent form at this trip and going, and a slight pace misjudgement by Anyasi's camp would make this a live scenario for the closers-in-waiting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace turns out stronger than expected, compressing the field and giving Red Legs a genuine late challenge.
scenarios.body: Red Legs, who races from the rear, would need the prominent horses to burn each other off ahead of her to generate any real momentum into the final furlong. Leicester's flat 6f is not especially generous to closers, so this is a low-probability scenario dependent on multiple things going wrong for the pace-setters simultaneously.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Retro Rocket or Baby G, both unknown quantities with limited form, show a natural racing style that catches the field unprepared.
scenarios.body: With just a handful of runs between them and uncertain running styles, either of these lightly-raced types could outrun their market price if they happen to sit in a perfect tactical position — though the absence of encouraging recent form and modest histories make this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Anyasi's rider Daniel Muscutt must judge the pace carefully — if she is allowed to bowl along too freely with no pressure, she may idle in front, handing a late challenge to Two Commanders or Bucklow Hill in the closing stages.

Bucklow Hill returns after 71 days off for Charles Hills; watch how sharply he moves to post and whether Sean Bowen opts to push him up prominently, which would be a positive sign that connections are confident about his fitness.

The two lightly-raced runners, Retro Rocket and Baby G, carry genuine behavioural uncertainty — either could jump awkwardly, miss the break, or interfere with other runners, disrupting the otherwise predictable early order.

Material Girl and Red Legs are both drawn in a field where the uncontested front-runner is OR 120 — if the pace is allowed to develop softly, both face the task of closing on a horse that has been given a completely free passage, making their task harder than their raw ratings suggest.

races.name: Rich And Carr Solicitors Handicap

runners_data.name: Kameel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on viable form (2nd over 10f on good recently, sim-going placed once in 15 attempts); Jessica Macey has a poor 14-day record (0/9) and 21 days fresh is fine, blinkers noted — dependent on late run finding traffic-free passage.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six runs, Kameel ran creditably when beaten three and a quarter lengths here last time off just a pound higher, and his best form comes on synthetic. This drop back in trip should suit, with a first-time visor and a 57 rating keeping him competitive.

runners_data.name: Hachiman
runners_data.note: Stepping up sharply from 8f to 10f here, a trip he has not raced over in recent history; Ruth Carr yard modest (1/20 in 14 days) and all recent runs on softer or standard going — the quicker Good to Firm conditions represent an untested dimension for a natural hold-up type.|
runners_data.comment: Held up in his races, Hachiman was never involved from a slow start when beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Doncaster last time, and he looks fully exposed since a flattering maiden success. His form claims are strongest over a mile, shorter than today's test, and with the stable out of form too, a 47 rating makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied; six-year-old with moderate recent form, all five recent runs in 8f-10f range on softer ground — Good to Firm is the firmest he has faced and that is a potential concern for a hold-up operator who needs everything to fall right.|
runners_data.comment: Below form of late, Charencey was beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Chepstow last time and has yet to win in five starts, with the stable also out of form. He does have course and distance form and acts on any going, and a first-time tongue-tie could help off a 55 rating.

runners_data.name: Beryl's Girl
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here with a recent 10f win on good ground confirming both trip and conditions; Eve Johnson Houghton has had 4 winners from 28 runners in 14 days, David Probert is a top-level pilot, and the P headgear confirms intent to bowl forward — conditions are tailor-made.|
runners_data.comment: Beryl's Girl arrives fresh from landing a handicap by two lengths at Brighton last time, showing much needed improvement once fitted with cheekpieces up to this trip. She acts well on a sound surface and rates the one to beat on a 63 rating, though a 5lb rise means she'll have to confirm that promise.

runners_data.name: City Escape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who shows consistent early prominence (E/S headgear); the most likely horse to give Beryl's Girl loose company up front without seriously threatening her, placed once in 15 similar-going runs — a useful stalker whose best hope is the leader running out of petrol.|
runners_data.comment: City Escape rates a strong threat on a 62 figure despite modest recent form, with an easing mark now working in her favour and this ten-furlong trip suiting on any going. She got over-excited and was below her best when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Bath last time, and that tendency, plus a first-time eyeshield to combat it, remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Bel Air Flyer
runners_data.note: Returned from a 68-day absence and fades in finish; three runs in, with two of those at 10f on good ground (9th both times) — while mapped to midfield, he is a genuine hold-up type whose style fit is weakened in a race short of late-race pace injection.|
runners_data.comment: Bel Air Flyer's best form is a fourth from three starts, with a shade more encouragement when down the field in a maiden at Lingfield last time. She may well improve now she tackles a handicap, but a 68-day absence and a 50 rating leave a fair bit to find.

runners_data.name: Argentum
runners_data.note: Trainer Matt Crawley has had 0 winners from 3 in the past fortnight; primarily a distance horse (12-16f in recent history) dropping back to 10f, and while P headgear shows some early intent, his best performances have come over longer trips — this may just be too sharp.|
runners_data.comment: Argentum had nothing more to give at an unsuitable fourteen furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Yarmouth last time, and she's still without a win in six starts. Today's ten furlongs is shorter than her best form around eleven to twelve, and although she acts on a sound surface, a 51 rating makes her tough to support.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground last time and has three placings from six runs at that trip in similar conditions — the most compelling hold-up profile in the field, even if mapped forward of his natural position; Jack Doughty's 7-day turnaround is fine and the form figures read well.|
runners_data.comment: A Daughters Love struck for the first time when landing a handicap by three and a quarter lengths at Chepstow last time, just seven days ago, and there should be more to come now she has that success under her belt. She stays this ten-furlong trip well on a sound surface and rates a serious threat on a 62 figure, though she does have to defy a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Arc At Her
runners_data.note: Three runs only, all at 8f, with two "fades in finish" flags — stepping up in trip here which may help, but the very limited profile (1 sim-going run) and Tyler Heard riding for a trainer with 1/21 in 14 days suggests she is unexposed rather than demonstrably effective at this level.|
runners_data.comment: A recent import from Ireland, Arc At Her looks sure to improve for a switch to handicaps, with her only sign of encouragement coming when down the field in a maiden at Lingfield last time after racing off the pace. She's rated a leading contender on 59, but her form to date is all on synthetic over nine furlongs, leaving today's ground and the step up in trip both unproven.

runners_data.name: Diamond Aura
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer in good form (4/32 in 14 days); handles Good to Firm ground (placed over 10f on similar recently), though P headgear last time did not produce a forward showing — mapped to midfield from a hold-up background, Sean Bowen an able booking if she does find her position.|
runners_data.comment: Diamond Aura ran to expectation when beaten four lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Brighton last time, and with the stable currently among the winners, she has a squeak if she builds on that. She's without a win in five starts and toils near the foot of the weights on a 53 rating, but she does act well on a sound surface over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Beryl's Girl is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 10-runner field on Good to Firm ground at Leicester over 1m2f, and with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her, David Probert can dictate a sustainable, unhurried tempo from the front. Her recent winning form at 10f on good ground confirms the trip and conditions suit, and an uncontested lead on a flat track with quick going is precisely the scenario that suits her profile. The field behind her is dominated by hold-up types — Kameel, Hachiman, Charencey, Bel Air Flyer, Argentum, A Daughters Love, Arc At Her and Diamond Aura — many of whom have been redistributed from the rear because the map cannot place them all at the back, but their natural style means they will be finishing from midfield or further back. City Escape is the only horse likely to press forward and offer any semblance of early company, but she is unlikely to seriously disrupt Beryl's Girl's rhythm. This race shape heavily favours the front-runner and any hold-up horse with a notably strong late kick on fast ground, though the lack of genuine pressing pace means the lead is unlikely to be run away from early — making a well-timed prominent or just-off-pace position the second most advantageous profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Beryl's Girl Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Beryl's Girl secures the lead uncontested and City Escape settles just behind without pressing.
scenarios.body: Beryl's Girl bowls along at a comfortable gallop on Good to Firm ground, dictating every yard and quickening when asked entering the straight; her winning form over 10f in similar conditions makes her ideally placed to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the hold-up horses generate enough momentum down the straight to overhaul the leader.
scenarios.body: A steady tempo sets up a sprint finish where horses with tactical speed from midfield benefit; A Daughters Love has won over 10f on good going recently and could produce the strongest late surge if the race truly sets up for closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If City Escape or another runner tracks Beryl's Girl closely and has more in reserve through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse travelling smoothly just off the pace would hit the front as Beryl's Girl's effort peaks, and City Escape's consistent placing profile at this trip suggests she is the likeliest beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is so dawdling that the field bunches and the race becomes a rough, unpredictable sprint for home.
scenarios.body: With 10 runners crowding midfield and multiple hold-up horses fighting for the same ground, the finish becomes untidy and a horse with a strong individual sprint and room to run could emerge from anywhere; Diamond Aura's Hugo Palmer yard is in form and she handles the going.

watchPoints.text: Beryl's Girl has no natural pace rival to push her — watch whether David Probert allows her to stride on or deliberately dawdles; if she dictates at a true pace, hold-up horses will struggle to close the gap on quick ground over 10f.

A Daughters Love ran just 7 days ago and is asked to back up quickly; watch in the paddock and early going for any signs of fatigue, as she is the hold-up horse with the most live credentials if fresh enough.

City Escape's early positioning will shape the race — if she pushes up to Beryl's Girl's girth rather than sitting off her, it could quicken the pace earlier than expected and open the race up for late closers in Scenario B or C.

Several redistributed hold-up horses (Bel Air Flyer, Argentum, Arc At Her, Diamond Aura) will be competing for the same ground in the straight — watch for crowding and interference between the two-furlong pole and the finish, particularly if the pace has been slow and the field is tightly grouped.

Kameel and Charencey both carry headgear (visor and tongue-tie respectively) and have going-concern flags on quicker surfaces — watch their early behaviour and whether either settles quickly, as resistance in the early stages could cost them lengths they cannot recover at this trip.

races.name: Curve Theatre Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lodge
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with solid similar-going form (2 wins/places from 5 on good or similar), but the 82-day absence is a flag and Brian Meehan's trainer-14 strike rate of 0/9 offers little confidence; needs the pace to be genuine to close from rear.
runners_data.comment: The form has gone in the wrong direction since a debut win, with this filly well beaten last time here having raced too freely and used up her energy too soon in a handicap; she returns for the first time in almost three months with a first-time tongue-tie fitted, and while she does act on this sort of ground, the leading form clearly poses a stern task.

runners_data.name: Dolo's Star
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old stepping up to 6f for the first time after three runs at 5f at Sandown — the extra furlong is an unknown quantity, and her form figures of 2-4-5 suggest consistency without a win yet.
runners_data.comment: A big-priced second in a novice at Southwell latest, beaten three quarters of a length, may have run above her true level that day, and there's a question over whether she can repeat it now stepping up to six furlongs on turf having previously been proven at the minimum trip on synthetic surfaces; she returns quickly after that break and sits bottom of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Carefree Dream
runners_data.note: Returned to form with back-to-back placed runs at 5f before this step up to 6f; holds up and has multiple placed efforts on good ground, but the trainer's 1/13 over 14 days and the distance extension temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Keen but game in defeat when beaten just a length off a slightly lower mark at Goodwood last time, this filly ran to form there and has been runner-up in each of her last two starts; she's clearly in good order right now and, with the figures suggesting she's effective down to five furlongs on any going, she's a leading player again off this mark.

runners_data.name: Guernsey Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form string of 4-6-5-6-6 tells a consistent story of near-misses and just-outside finishes; course and distance form is absent and the pattern suggests she finds one or two too good.
runners_data.comment: Comfortably held back up at six furlongs in a handicap at Haydock last time, this filly didn't see out the trip fully there, continuing a run of modest finishes without ever threatening; she does act well on quick ground or all-weather, but more is clearly needed to get involved in this company.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Aleen
runners_data.note: Marco Botti firing (3/15 T14) and she is the more accomplished of the two confirmed front-runners — has placed on good ground at 7f but drops back to 6f here, and her ability to control the race from the front is the key tactical question for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Not seeing out a step up to a mile on soft ground when a close third at Lingfield most recently, this filly has otherwise gone well in maiden company, placing once more before that; back closer to her best trip with first-time cheekpieces added, she can't be ruled out on her first attempt at a handicap.

runners_data.name: Q T Pie
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's filly has a win and a place from five runs on good or similar, and her 1-win effort came over 6f on good ground — her profile suits a prominently-ridden horse in a truly-run sprint, and William Carson's booking adds jockey confidence.
runners_data.comment: A revival of form saw her beaten just half a length off a lighter mark at Goodwood last time, and that comeback run, her first of the season, should bring improvement with a race under her belt; effective at today's trip on this sort of ground as a two-year-old, she rates a leading contender again.

runners_data.name: Amelia's Joy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form, though all five recent runs have been at 7f and the drop to 6f on faster ground is a legitimate query; David Probert's booking and the trainer's active recent form (3/10 T14) are positives.
runners_data.comment: Splitting two wins either side of a handful of minor-place finishes, this filly continues to race to a fair level, and was beaten just half a length last time off a mark of sixty-two, only a pound lower than today; the yard is in good form, first-time cheekpieces are added, and she looks competitive again at a trip she handles well.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sue
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at sprint distances, but this is a horse whose true style is hold-up racing — crowded out to a midfield map position by the volume of hold-up types in this field, meaning she is unlikely to get her natural position; STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers her chance.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Redcar last time but running to her level there, this filly has a workable, easing mark in her favour today, and first-time cheekpieces could sharpen her up further; she's suited by this trip on quick or soft ground, giving her a fair chance if she can find more.

runners_data.name: May Encounter
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's five-year-old has struggled for a win (0W from 8 on similar going) and her form string of 5-5-5-6-4 paints a picture of a pace-setter who sets the table for others; she will press for the lead but is more likely to be the sacrificial front-runner than the winner.
runners_data.comment: A modest effort at Nottingham last time, beaten three lengths from a mark two pounds higher than today, leaves this filly something of an unknown quantity on recent evidence, having failed to add to a run of similar finishing positions beforehand; she should be suited by this trip on a sound surface, but the case for her remains unclear.

runners_data.name: Spacewoman
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground last time out and her hold-up style is authentic, though she is genuinely crowded into a midfield mapping position here — the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 is a minor discount, but her recent winning form at this trip and going is the standout recent performance in the field.
runners_data.comment: A neck victory down to six furlongs at Newmarket last time, off a mark four pounds lower than today, marked this filly's first success and came after finding herself suited by a drop in trip; she looks open to further progress still as an out-and-out sprinter, remains unexposed at the trip, and heads this field on our figures despite stamina beyond six furlongs still unproven.

runners_data.name: Grand Citadel
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with strong course form (1W, 4P from 8 on good at Leicester and similar), wears a hood, and recent form includes a win at 7f on good — drops back to 6f which may slightly test her stamina profile, but the course and going familiarity is a genuine edge.
runners_data.comment: A well-held tenth back down to six furlongs last time, beaten ten lengths off the same mark she races off today, was a big step back for this mare after an earlier spell of form that had brought a win among some encouraging placed efforts; first-time blinkers are added in the hope of a return to form, and she does act across a wide range of trips and going.

races.paceDynamic: Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter are the two confirmed front-runners in this 11-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Leicester, and with both likely to push for the early lead, the pace should be genuinely contested and honest from the outset. Sayidah Aleen has the class edge and a more active trainer in form (3/15 over 14 days), making her the likelier pace-setter, while May Encounter will press hard from alongside, meaning neither is simply allowed to bowl along unchallenged. Guernsey Angel and Q T Pie will be close to the pace from prominent positions, adding further pressure to the front end and ensuring the gallop does not relax in the middle stages. This race shape — a truly run sprint with no let-up — will favour hold-up and late-finishing profiles that can benefit from a strong pace to aim at, though the redistribution caveat is important: Sierra Sue and Spacewoman are genuine hold-up types whose natural rear-ground position is compromised by the volume of hold-up horses in this field, and it is Spacewoman (recent 6f winner on good) and Lodge (proven on similar going) who are best placed to occupy true back-marker roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Sayidah Aleen and May Encounter fight for supremacy and burn each other off, setting a genuine strong pace throughout.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop from two front-runners on good-to-firm ground drains those at the head of affairs and opens the race up for horses coming with a late run from off the pace. Genuine hold-up horses Lodge and Spacewoman are best positioned to exploit this, with the latter's recent 6f win on good ground making her particularly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners cancel each other out and the pace proves honest but not scorching, allowing prominent racers to travel sweetly.
scenarios.body: Q T Pie and Amelia's Joy, both proven in similar conditions, can sit just off the early battle, travel kindly and hit the line hard without having used excessive energy. Q T Pie's course form (1 win, 1 place on good) and Amelia's Joy's recent placed run on good give both an edge in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sayidah Aleen (or May Encounter) gets an uncontested lead or the early duel quickly resolves in one horse's favour.
scenarios.body: Should one pace-setter establish dominance quickly and the other back off, the winner sets a controlled gallop and simply doesn't get caught, using the good-to-firm ground to sustain their effort over the final furlong. Sayidah Aleen, trained by the in-form Marco Botti (3/15 over 14 days), is the more likely beneficiary of this shape given her class edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively moderate and the race bunches, negating the advantage of horses coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A condensed, slowly-run sprint would compress the field and reward those in prominent positions who never had to fight for their spot, leaving true hold-up types with no gaps to exploit late. Lodge and Sierra Sue, both operating from the rear, would be the biggest losers in this shape, while Grand Citadel's course and distance form on good ground makes her the standout beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sayidah Aleen or May Encounter establishes early supremacy — if neither backs down in the first furlong, the pace will be fierce and both are likely to be spent by the 2f pole, opening the door wide for Spacewoman and Lodge.

Spacewoman is mapped to midfield but is a genuine hold-up horse — watch her draw and early positioning in-running, as her STYLE_FIT flag means she may struggle to get back to her preferred position if the field is compact.

Grand Citadel's course record at Leicester on good ground (8 runs, 1 win, 4 places) is unusually strong for a horse at this level — watch if she is allowed to track the pace from a prominent position, as she has done her best work in exactly that scenario here.

Q T Pie's only win came at 6f on good ground — if she travels smoothly in behind the early pace battle and William Carson times the challenge between the 2f and 1f poles, her profile fits the most probable race shape almost perfectly.

Lodge's 82-day absence is worth monitoring in the betting market — if the market contracts significantly for her pre-race, it may signal that Brian Meehan's yard has her in peak condition despite the lay-off, which would make her hold-up profile from the rear much more dangerous.

races.name: KLG Rutland Handicap

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Fanshawe with strong form over this course and distance on good ground (1W2P in sim-going), stepping back up to seven furlongs where he scored last time; the sole confirmed pace-setter whose uncontested lead is the axis around which the entire race shape revolves — his style fit here is strong.
runners_data.comment: Fifth when not staying a mile at Goodwood last time, he still ran to his mark for much of it, and a drop back to seven furlongs suits after a win and two places in his last five starts; he carries top weight but with the yard in form, he rates the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Galileo Island
runners_data.note: Botti-trained three-year-old who has placed three times in five career starts and recorded a win over today's trip on good ground; sits naturally in the prominent group and is well placed to exploit the controlled tempo if he travels with his usual fluency — a genuine contender to pounce on Mr Writer late.
runners_data.comment: A below-form eighth at Doncaster last time reflected a stamina issue in a competitive handicap rather than a loss of ability, following a solid recent sequence that included a win and two further places; first-time cheekpieces and a return to seven furlongs, a trip he handles well, should help turn that form around.

runners_data.name: Cashbox
runners_data.note: Hills runner with back-to-back wins on his form string but two recent disappointing efforts at this course and distance; carries headgear (p) and steps up to prominent racing on good-to-firm ground where his best form was recorded, though the back-to-back blanks at Leicester demand explanation before elevating his chance.
runners_data.comment: Below-par again when beaten five lengths in a handicap at Sandown last time, this is now two runs without a repeat of the form that brought a pair of wins, and a return to form is overdue; cheekpieces go on for the first time and he does act well at this trip on a sound surface, but our figures rate him one of the more vulnerable in this field.

runners_data.name: Loquella
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up three-year-old returning from a 64-day absence, which is the most notable flag here; her natural style is to come from off the pace and the lack of recent competitive sharpness after two months off tempers expectations, though the Good to Firm and seven furlongs suit her profile if fit.
runners_data.comment: A fifth in a handicap at Newcastle last time, below the level she showed in novice company and beaten five lengths, arrives over two months since that run; she's normally suited by a sharper six furlongs than today's test, though she does act on this surface, and with more needed on the balance of that form, she's up against it in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Pints In Peace
runners_data.note: Furtado runner whose recent form shows no wins or places on good-ground equivalents (0W0P in sim-going), and whose trainer has shown no wins from 20 runners over 14 days; races from a hold-up position and would need a genuine test to fire, but the going and form evidence both work against him at this level.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten seventh last time from a higher mark of 77, some way below his level on that occasion, this gelding still holds a pair of wins in his last six starts and races off a more workable 72 today; a first-time tongue-tie could aid focus, and he handles quick and soft ground alike, though there's a little more to prove back on turf.

runners_data.name: Frantic
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old has a natural front-running profile but, with a busier early pack, is expected to get shuffled out of that berth — the horse races from further back than it would prefer, which dilutes the value of its solid placed form on good ground; watch for whether it actually contests the lead from stall.
runners_data.comment: A luckless seventh last time, only beaten three lengths off her current mark despite not enjoying the run of the race, arrives on the back of three runner-up finishes and a fourth in her other recent starts; well suited by this trip on any surface, she rates a fair chance again among the principals.

runners_data.name: Eduardo Calderon
runners_data.note: Eustace-trained three-year-old who is genuinely a hold-up type in terms of racing style, though the map places him in midfield due to field compression; has placed twice on good-going equivalents but returns from 44 days off for a yard with just one winner from four runs in the past fortnight — will need everything to drop right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: A fourth in a handicap at Haydock last time, beaten six lengths and true to his level there, sits on the back of a mixed campaign that includes a runner-up effort among the placings; a six-week absence hasn't dimmed the promise of more to offer under handicap conditions, and he's effective at this trip on quick and soft ground alike.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slot comfortably into an uncontested position from the gates, dictating a sustainable Good to Firm gallop over seven furlongs at Leicester. Galileo Island, Cashbox, and Mr Writer itself form a cluster of prominent-style horses competing for the front rank, meaning the actual pace will be honest but not frantic — a rhythm that rewards those who travel within themselves. The field contains more prominent types than the map can accommodate: Frantic is a genuine front-runner pushed into a midfield position on the map, while Eduardo Calderon is a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield due to cluster compression, so neither is guaranteed to race in its preferred shape. A controlled but legitimate pace with a single dominant pace-setter setting terms strongly favours the prominent-to-mid-division profile: horses that can sit just off the early tempo, cover the ground on the good-to-firm surface, and produce a sustained gallop rather than a late sprint kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer dictates an uncontested rhythm and the prominent horses track efficiently, setting up a true run to the line.
scenarios.body: Mr Writer bowls along on a fair but comfortable fractions, with Galileo Island and Cashbox in close attendance; the race becomes a sustained stamina test on Good to Firm ground that plays directly into front-rank travellers who stay the seven furlongs well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer is headed entering the final quarter-mile and a tracking prominent horse produces the strongest finishing effort.
scenarios.body: The early pace proves just quick enough to string the field out, and a horse like Galileo Island or Cashbox, settled just off the leader, unleashes a clean turn-of-foot on the sound surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly honest and the front rank ties each other up, allowing a genuine hold-up runner to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Loquella, as the most authentic hold-up type in the field, would need to cover ground efficiently from a rear position; on Good to Firm over seven furlongs at Leicester the final two furlongs can be sharp enough to reward a late run if the leaders have burned energy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Frantic Seizes Front
scenarios.trigger: If Frantic — a natural front-runner squeezed out of position on the map — actually breaks sharply and contests the early lead, injecting more pace than anticipated.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would increase the overall tempo and benefit true hold-up horses, but Frantic racing against Mr Writer for the lead risks burning out both principals; this scenario is less likely because Frantic is mapped out of its natural role and the price of a pace duel is significant.

watchPoints.text: Mr Writer (front-runner) breaking cleanly and establishing an uncontested lead — if he gets out and across without pressure from Frantic, the race shape is set immediately in his favour.

Frantic's behaviour in the early furlongs: if it contests the pace with Mr Writer rather than dropping into midfield as the map projects, the tempo will lift materially and the entire probability balance shifts toward hold-up horses.

Loquella's freshness after 64 days off — a hold-up runner returning from a layoff on quick ground needs to travel fluently from the outset; any early signs of reluctance or lack of sharpness will end her chance before the straight.

Cashbox's headgear (p) combined with two poor recent runs at this venue: if the gear change sparks a markedly improved early response and she settles prominently, she re-enters the equation — watch her behaviour in the initial two furlongs.

Eduardo Calderon's positioning in the first two furlongs — as a genuine hold-up type compressed onto the map at midfield, if the field strings out quickly on Good to Firm ground he may find himself too far back too soon to make an impact from his mapped position.

races.name: Appliance City Bunny 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Palmarian
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Ruth Carr and James Sullivan, with six runs in form showing multiple placed efforts at 7f on Good; steps up to 1m for the first time in this sequence which is a query, though sim-going figures (5 from 12 on comparable ground) suggest the surface is fine — lacks a natural prominence here but could sit handy if things go smoothly.
runners_data.comment: Palmarian ran up to his level when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Redcar last time, undone by racing too freely again, and he remains without a win in six starts. He has course and distance form in the book, but stretching out beyond his sharper seven-furlong form is a query, and with a first-time hood, a stable out of form, and a 60 rating, he's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: My Ambition
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's seven-year-old has placed twice at 8f on Firm and Standard and arrives on a 53-day break; a genuine closer by instinct who will need the race to truly run to suit, and with several rivals sharing the same preference, finding clear air late will be a tactical headache.
runners_data.comment: My Ambition showed solid form when runner-up and third in two of his last three starts, before an underwhelming effort when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Bath last time, undone by racing too freely. Back after 53 days, he gets his conditions over this mile on a sound surface and rates a major player on 74, though there's a risk he takes too strong a hold again if he fails to settle.

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and sole pace anchor — won at Yarmouth in July, goes on tapfast ground, and Ashley Lewis (5lb claim) reduces the weight; the 54-day absence is a genuine risk but the tactical situation is entirely in its favour if it travels well.
runners_data.comment: Aspire To Glory has little to recommend him on recent evidence, having been below form again when down the field in a handicap at Wolverhampton latest, and he's managed only one win in his last five starts. He does act well on an easy surface or the all-weather over today's trip, but back after a break of 54 days and up against sharper types, a 60 rating looks about right.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's nine-year-old is fresh off a run just nine days ago and has two places from fifteen on comparable going; David Allan aboard is a booking of note — naturally a hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by the busy field composition, so a clear run rather than position will determine its fate.
runners_data.comment: Little Ted heads the market on our figures, having gone down by only a head at Newcastle last time from a mark 2lb lower than today's. He's proven at this trip and on sound ground, and building on that narrow defeat, a rating of 79 makes him the one to beat, with a want of a win in six starts his only real query.

runners_data.name: Aurelune
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Richard and Peter Fahey having only run on Soft and Standard so far; Harry Russell rides and the drop back from 10f is worth a second look, but the lack of any Good or Firm ground form is an uncertain factor on today's surface.
runners_data.comment: Aurelune managed little up at ten furlongs when well beaten in a handicap at Nottingham last time, and she remains without a win in four starts. Back to a trip within her best 7-9f range and on a sound surface, she has conditions in her favour, but a 60 rating and a wide draw leave her work cut out.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Bright
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has placed three times from ten on Good or Standard ground and returned placed at 10f last time; Daniel Muscutt provides a quality booking and the horse's ability to race prominently makes it a natural beneficiary of an uncontested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Bright rates a big player back down to a mile having raced too freely up at ten furlongs when beaten nine lengths in a handicap at Wetherby last time. First-time cheekpieces could help settle her, and she goes well on quicker ground or the all-weather, giving her claims on a rating of 76, though she needs to find better than that below-par effort.

runners_data.name: Avispado
runners_data.note: David Menuisier sends this three-year-old out with a trainer who is 3 from 11 over 14 days — a meaningful angle; naturally a hold-up performer whose best run on good ground (4th, 8f) came in similar conditions, but Kaiya Fraser will need a gap that may not materialise easily with so many closers in the field.
runners_data.comment: Avispado did have his excuses when fourth, beaten eight lengths in a handicap at this course last time, with the form working out better than the bare result suggests. He remains without a win in four starts and sits bottom of the field on a 58 rating, but conditions over today's trip suit and the yard is in good form, while a wide draw is a complication.

runners_data.name: Stole My Heart
runners_data.note: David Evans's three-year-old has shown modest form in a string of 6f-7f handicaps on Standard, with only one relevant comparable-going run (3rd, 7f, Standard); Pat Cosgrave is an experienced hand but the horse is at the top end of its form range on current evidence and steps up in trip.
runners_data.comment: Stole My Heart ran up to expectations when third, beaten seven and a quarter lengths in a handicap at Wolverhampton last time, despite showing signs it wasn't straightforward. She's a fair yardstick for this level on her day and rates a threat on 67, though stepping up beyond her sharper 6-7f form and a lack of a win in five starts leave a question mark.

runners_data.name: Leia Antilles
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's three-year-old, partnered by Sean D Bowen, has finished placed at 8f on Good twice but the overall record on Good going (4 runs, no wins or places from this surface specifically) gives pause; lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 47, and the trip and going combination are the main positives.
runners_data.comment: Leia Antilles showed better form down at this mile trip when cheekpieces were fitted last time, finishing fourth, beaten seven lengths, in a handicap at Bath. She's suited by good ground over today's distance and has a squeak if she builds further, but she remains without a win in five starts and is up against sharper types on 62.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest early supremacy, will be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Leicester. That lone-pace scenario means the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, which will compress the field and reduce the advantage for genuine hold-up horses needing a strongly-run race to close into. The race shape strongly favours Aspire To Glory if it can replicate its Yarmouth win, and more broadly rewards any runner able to sit close to the pace in a prominent position and travel through the race without expending extra energy. Closers and hold-up profiles are structurally disadvantaged here because the pace that would normally string the field out and create a true test does not exist. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than can occupy natural rear positions — My Ambition, Avispado, Stole My Heart, Leia Antilles, and Little Ted are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield in the map, meaning several will be racing out of their preferred role and cannot all find a clean passage late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire To Glory Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory breaks cleanly and is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged at a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: Aspire To Glory sets a tempo it controls entirely, conserves energy through the turn, and simply needs to find enough to hold on as rivals make their belated efforts; the Good to Firm ground suits and a 54-day break is the only concern, partially offset by Dylan Cunha's recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory's lead is tracked closely by a prominent-sitting rival who times a challenge to peak at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A horse travelling just off the pace in second or third position benefits from the compressed, slowly-run nature of the race and overpowers a tiring front-runner in the final furlong; Sovereign Bright's ability to race prominently on good ground and Palmarian's tendency to sit handy make both credible in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Enough Room
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and creates sufficient gaps for a closing run down the outside in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Despite the structural disadvantage, a hold-up horse that has been pushed forward by the redistribution effect and manages a cleaner run than rivals could benefit if Aspire To Glory ties up; Little Ted's recent placed form at 8f on similar ground and My Ambition's consistency at this trip are the best credentials in this profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead early, unsettling Aspire To Glory and turning the race into a rough, contested affair.
scenarios.body: A scrappy pace scramble would muddy all positional calculations, potentially allowing a fresh-legged horse at the back to benefit from a chaotic final furlong; Avispado's trainer David Menuisier shows strong 14-day form and the gelding's good-ground run at 8f gives it an outside claim in a messy scenario.

watchPoints.text: Aspire To Glory's jumping gate cleanly — if it dwells or gets shuffled back in the early stages, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the race becomes genuinely unpredictable for all runners.

Multiple hold-up horses (Little Ted, My Ambition, Avispado, Leia Antilles, Stole My Heart) will be queuing for the same late ground on the outside — watch for traffic problems and interference in the final two furlongs that could cost any one of them.
Sovereign Bright's ability to track Aspire To Glory in second or third is the key positional battle to monitor at the start; if it secures that berth it becomes the main threat to the leader.

Aurelune has never raced on Good to Firm or similar fast ground — monitor in the market and paddock for any signs the Fahey team are confident the horse handles the surface before weighting its chance.

David Menuisier's 3-from-11 trainer form over 14 days is a live angle for Avispado, but its redistribution into a midfield role means it needs an unusually clean trip to translate that stable form into a result.

races.name: Bunches Handicap

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lass
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good last time and holds solid course form; natural hold-up style means she will need the race to set up for a sustained late run, and visor headgear could sharpen her focus through the final stages.
runners_data.comment: Moonhall Lass arrives in tremendous form, striking last time when landing a handicap by two and a quarter lengths here fitted with a visor, backed up by three wins from her last six starts overall. She goes on quick ground over this trip and rates a big threat on 67, though she does have to defy a 4lb rise having claimed that prize from an easier mark.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with three third-place finishes on good going — a naturally prominent racer who should travel sweetly just off Rianka's heels and represents the clearest positional fit for this pace shape; trainer in quiet form at T14 0/2.
runners_data.comment: Elvetham has a win and three thirds among his last six starts, but he needs to put a well-beaten twelfth last time behind him, easier now by a pound. Effective at this trip, and with conditions no worries on any ground, first-time blinkers could be the key to rediscovering better form, and he still rates a threat on 60.

runners_data.name: Due Date
runners_data.note: Carries genuine hold-up tendencies, though the compressed field will prevent settling as far back as preferred; long 59-day absence and a run of seven-place finishes on standard ground make this a qualifying run rather than a winning one.
runners_data.comment: Due Date has struggled to be competitive in six starts without a win, running to form when beaten four lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Kempton last time. He does drop in the weights today and gets his ideal conditions over this sprint trip on a sound surface, but a lengthy 59-day gap and a first-time visor add to the uncertainty on a modest 49 rating.

runners_data.name: Melissa Honey
runners_data.note: Showed good form on good ground including a win and second place, and her handler is in reasonable nick (T14 3/10); her true closer's profile is squeezed by the crowded midfield, so she'll need a well-timed run through horses rather than a clean outside passage.
runners_data.comment: Melissa Honey confirmed her improvement when a close second, beaten only half a length, last time out, backing up a win from two starts back, and she remains on a workable mark for another bold bid. She's suited by this trip on quick ground or the all-weather, the stable is in form, and she rates a big threat on 67 up just a pound.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Ran only five days ago and a quick back-up on a young three-year-old is a concern; hold-up style suits only if the pace truly stretches, and a record of 0 wins from five runs on good ground limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Great Success was below his best when beaten three lengths off this same mark at Pontefract last time, faltering without response in the closing stages, and he remains without a win in five starts. He is suited by this trip on fast ground or synthetic, though he needs to reverse that form quickly on a five-day turnaround to make an impact on 60.

runners_data.name: Bridget's Baby
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good recently and is stepping up in trip — her closer's instincts are naturally compressed into midfield here, and apprentice rider Myla Coppins (7lb claim) could help offset her wide draw if she finds a position.
runners_data.comment: Bridget's Baby heads the market having broken her duck readily, landing a handicap by two lengths at Lingfield last time with distance to spare. A 5lb rise is the obvious query, but she's proven at today's course, distance and going, and rates the one to beat on 69 as she continues to progress.

runners_data.name: Rianka
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and pace-setter throughout; good to firm ground is fine, though her form reads 8-5-4-7 and she has yet to win — her best chance is if she can dictate a controlled tempo and last home rather than being run down by better-handicapped rivals.
runners_data.comment: Rianka failed to settle and lacked the pace to finish her race when beaten five and a half lengths in a handicap at Windsor last time, and she remains without a win in four starts. A first-time tongue-tie could help settle her, and the step up to this six-furlong trip on quicker ground looks a definite plus, but a 47 rating leaves her with plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Rianka is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control the tempo from the gates on good to firm ground over six furlongs at Leicester. The pace is likely to be honest rather than suicidal — Rianka sets a sustainable rhythm and dictates throughout, which on a flat, quick-ground track strongly favours horses who can travel in the slipstream and pick up in the final two furlongs rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the back — Due Date, Bridget's Baby, and Melissa Honey are all genuine closers who will be competing for space in midfield rather than settling into their natural positions. This race shape, with a single uncontested lead and a compressed midfield, gives the clearest tactical advantage to prominent-to-midfield horses who can hold a handy berth and pounce from two furlongs out without needing a seam to open late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rianka Dictates, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Rianka bowls along at a fair but controlled gallop and the compressed midfield produces a straight-line sprint from two out.
scenarios.body: Rianka's uncontested lead on quick ground means she sets the terms, and horses settled in second or third position — notably Elvetham — are ideally placed to pounce without burning energy fighting for cover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Rianka Hangs On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Rianka's pace proves genuinely strong enough and she conserves enough to repel all challengers inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: At a one-paced gallop on good to firm with no pressure, Rianka has an uninterrupted run through and her light weight and forward position allow her to hold off the advancing pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Swoopers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens from the halfway point and the midfield compresses, leaving daylight for horses to deliver late runs.
scenarios.body: Moonhall Lass and Great Success, though mapping to the rear, would benefit if the race slows early and suddenly quickens, creating the late-run scenario that suits their closing profiles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Rianka goes off too fast too soon and the field regroups turning for home in a chaotic scramble.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse would theoretically bring the redistributed hold-up horses — Due Date, Bridget's Baby, Melissa Honey — back into it, but since none will be in their true natural position, any benefit is structurally compromised and a blanket finish remains the least predictable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Elvetham is ideally placed to travel in Rianka's slipstream throughout — if she tracks the leader cleanly and pounces at the two-furlong pole she is the primary danger to the entire field in this shape.

Rianka's front-running profile is uncontested but her form figures of 8-5-4 suggest she has consistently flattered to deceive — watch for signs of weakening inside the final furlong if the pace has been too quick.

Due Date has not run for 59 days and all recent form was recorded on standard Tapeta — the switch back to quick turf after a near two-month break is a significant unknown and could see her outpaced early.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Due Date, Bridget's Baby, Melissa Honey — will all be bunched in midfield; watch for traffic problems or riders having to check and switch at the two-furlong marker where the track narrows.

Great Success ran just five days ago — watch for any signs of a flat performance or lack of acceleration, as back-to-back quick turnarounds for an unexposed three-year-old on this ground is an obvious stamina and freshness query.
